summary: High-performing videos by views and stayed_pct rely on concise titles under 45 characters that use direct paradoxes rather than generic questions.
The first sentence of top-tier videos immediately subverts common physical assumptions with a direct, declarative statement rather than filler words.
Videos with low stayed_pct (below 35%) suffer from asking predictable questions or leaning on stale emojis instead of creating an urgent knowledge gap.
Length correlates heavily with drop-off; under-performing videos exceeding 30 seconds experienced massive audience attrition in the initial feed test.
Channel distribution stalls predictably unless the initial hook establishes a counterintuitive visual or logical contradiction within the first 3 seconds.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
Ever noticed those tiny black dots fading around your car windshield? 🚗
avoid: Starting a hook with a polite question like 'Have you ever wondered...'
Using long conversational introductions that delay the core paradox past the 3-second mark
Writing vague titles that do not immediately communicate the physical stakes or weirdness
Exceeding 30 seconds of runtime before establishing the payoff
next_experiment: Test two identical topics comparing a declarative physiological contradiction hook ('Your skin does X because Y') versus a direct question hook ('Why does your skin do X?'), measuring stayed_pct at the 3-second mark.
